correctness.rationale: For the homogeneous invariant two-group sector, d=t(1-x)/(1+t) and x=s exp(-u). Integration gives u=(r/t)log[(1+t)/(1+t x)] for active and u=r(1-x)/(1+t) for fixed incidence. Unique positive fixed points follow from strict concavity and boundedness. The analytic expansion in epsilon=1/t gives active coefficient sr log(1/s)-(1-s), fixed coefficient (1-s)(sr-1); on r=(1-s)/(s log(1/s)) the active second coefficient is -(1-s)^2/(2s). Since log(1/s)>1-s, the wedge is nonempty; analytic remainders give the eventual opposite derivative and sidedness. Endpoint d_active(t)->0 as t->0 plus continuity and finite excess gives an attained finite positive maximum, not uniqueness. Independently recomputed coefficients with SymPy and fixed points numerically at s=1/2,r=3/2,t=100,1000,10000.
